gate: Watch a person carrying this code make a case for something they actually want. There is a slight lean, a shift in cadence, the small confident exaggeration that turns a flat fact into something a listener will pick up and carry home. The drive is to pitch, to frame, to take a thing and present it so another person reaches for it. This code carries the salesman's energy and the storyteller's slant. There is muscle in it, the muscle of the small triangle off the right side of the chart. The misread is that this is manipulation, hype, ego strut. Sometimes it is. The clean expression is closer to advocacy. The case lands because the body behind it actually believes the thing being said. Where it goes sour is when it sells what it does not believe, or sells to fill an empty pocket rather than to feed the tribe. The integrity question lives inside the pitch itself.
centre_field: The Will Center is the smallest shape on the body-map, a little red triangle tucked off to the right side. Smallness is part of the teaching. This is one of the four motors, and it concerns itself almost entirely with the material world, the world of value and capacity, of saying a thing and doing it. Roughly a third of people have this center defined, yet everyone is asked to behave as if they do. That cultural pressure is a key piece of what this gate runs into. The gate sits as one of the four outlets from this motor, the one pointed at the tribe. So the placement says, plainly, that the pitch is a willpower function. It costs energy. The motor works to rest, and when it skips the resting half it burns out, and burned out, the voice loses its conviction. The pitch needs the rest behind it.
channel: Pitch without instinct becomes hype. That is the structural problem this code lives inside. Alone, the egoic motor can talk anyone into anything, including things that will harm them, including things that will harm the speaker. It has volume but no warning system. The reach is toward the gate of alertness, in the spleen, the body's old survival sense. The two together form what the lineage calls the channel of surrender, sometimes the channel of transmission. The spleen end supplies the gut read, the felt yes or no on whether a thing is actually good for the tribe to take in. Joined, the pitch carries something that has already passed a health check. Selling becomes a kind of service. Without that partner, this code is a megaphone with no listener inside it. Built into the wiring is the need for an instinct it does not contain.
